geometry_edits.rationale: Wrap the current dominant mass with a courtyard operator to convert the sealed prism into a street-responsive neighborhood form.
Create a clear but controlled void while preserving the dominant building figure.
Orient the court opening toward the programmed access side so the frontage becomes active and legible.

graph_edits.rationale: Retarget the dominant mass to create a real public court/void so the street edge becomes legible instead of sealed.
Keep the void modest so the main mass remains dominant while still opening a usable threshold.
Open the court toward the access side to align the public void with arrival and frontage.

rationale: The mass is coherent in all views and the non-rectangular plan helps, but it still reads as a sealed compact object with only a weakly articulated ground edge. The blue access edge is not answered by a legible void, notch, or undercut, so the public threshold remains unresolved. The silhouette is acceptable as an early massing gesture, but the section is too generic for neighborhood living: no clear active ground, no meaningful terrace/court consequence, and the upper shaping does not yet establish a strong program hierarchy. Visually it resembles a compact prism/tower fragment more than a neighborhood street building, so program fit fails on relationship logic rather than style.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is much taller and more overtly tower-like; the candidate is a small block and currently lacks the public threshold and mixed-use ground expression that make the precedent work.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact mixed-use prism with a readable stepped/tapered upper mass can work when the ground and section stay program-legible.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate does not yet have the open canopy/cut/entry seam that gives this reference its public street response.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A low, calm street-facing base with a distinct attached vertical/accent element can support neighborhood-serving frontage when the ground edge is active.

warnings: Parcel containment appears satisfied, but the access edge response is semantically weak.
Do not over-credit the tapered top; it does not yet produce usable public space or section logic.
The form is readable in four views, so the main issue is program/threshold fit, not structural incoherence.
